evidence.claim: Narration immediately describes palm on table, chisel strike and severed ring finger.
Severed digit and late wife wedding ring are offered in exchange for underworld protection.
The wider assassin background, hotel rule and 14-million-dollar bounty are introduced after the opening bargain and suit.
One-hour head start is established, later expires at the clinic and forces the doctor to stop.
Concierge request and response interrupt the narration.
limitations: ASR transcribes a possibly incorrect name as Mr. Wythe; speaker source not auditioned.

evidence.claim: Deadline and money exchange is presented as apparent character conversation.
limitations: ASR merges multiple turns and has uncertain wording.

evidence.claim: Good luck, Mr. Wick and Thanks, Doc appear near the clinic departure.
limitations: ASR gap is not proof of silence.

evidence.claim: Closing narration says assassins swarm again because the bounty remains active.
Last inspected samples continue the clinic exit and street threat with compact captions, without a generic end card.
limitations: Nominal one-second sample labels; not every final frame inspected.

evidence.claim: Opening preparation scrubs skin with a steel brush; stadium-cash target is explained later.
You called 911 question appears during the disguised-police arrival.
Ending transitions to another bank robbery after the earlier escape.
Five locks and an upside-down cup precede the wealthy-hitman/poor-flat contradiction and hidden room.
Accepted job is later revealed as a trap, followed by an unexpected second arrival.
Last automatic segment ends at 152.41 seconds, approximately 6.90 seconds before file end.
limitations: Untranscribed tail may contain speech, effects or other material; not audited.

evidence.claim: Rifle maker discovers the client aims his weapon at him, then explains how he sabotaged it.
limitations: Technical weapon claims and story details are not independently verified.

evidence.claim: Wounded protagonist meets girlfriend and reflects on a simple happy life.
Reference calls the target dead on the spot then barely alive in successive passages.
limitations: Potential reference narration or ASR inconsistency; verify before reuse.

evidence.claim: An amulet/spirit conversation precedes narrator setup of fighters and revenge.
limitations: Speaker source inferred pending audition.

evidence.claim: Escalation is organized into different fighting phases: mismatch, glass wraps, weapons and comeback.
Victory, brother avenged, goodbye and new life resolve the central fight.
Late samples show fight close-ups, a triumphant fighter, supporters and departure on a boat.
limitations: Four-second sampling and nominal labels; not exact event timestamps.

evidence.claim: Extended police argument includes killing a suspect and a broken dash recorder.
limitations: Quoted character views are not endorsed facts; exact source dialogue requires audition.

evidence.claim: Nick reaches a new understanding after an armed traffic-stop crisis.
Camera avoidance, accidental exposure and intelligence-service identification set up the pursuit.
First team is defeated but another assassin is dispatched.
Skilled shooter deliberately appears weak before revenge backstory explains his new job.
Police know the protagonist identity but keep it quiet, leaving dramatic irony unresolved.
Narrated annual, monthly and daily robbery figures do not agree arithmetically.
limitations: Do not repeat statistics as verified facts.

evidence.claim: Representative samples show compact uppercase white captions with a bold italic appearance, generally one or two lines centered in the central-lower image region.
limitations: Estimated baseline around 60–65% of frame height; not exact font or pixel measurement.
Static sheets cannot establish exact word-emphasis animation.

evidence.claim: Representative samples fill the square with movie footage, faces and story-specific objects.
limitations: Sampling cannot exclude brief cards or overlays elsewhere.
Original crop and added camera movements require source-film comparison.

evidence.claim: Visible hands, ring, preparation equipment, hidden room, rifle parts, fight equipment, gloves, cameras/traps and robbery bags correspond to concrete transcript actions.
limitations: Representative semantic correspondence, not certified frame-level audio/video alignment.

evidence.claim: The corpus supports renewed-threat, reflective, resolved and thematic endings; a universal cliffhanger template would overfit.
Extreme opening action precedes wider causal history by about 31 seconds; the production planner needs cold-open and chronological-reset support.

suggested_profile.status: Initial implementation choices, not recovered creator settings.
suggested_profile.planning_rate_caveat: Not isolated narrator pace; synthesize and measure actual speech, reserving source dialogue and action time.
suggested_profile.audio_policy_caveat: Clean-output choice; louder references have positive measured true peaks that should not be copied.
suggested_profile.shot_length_policy: Variable semantic edits; scene detector intervals are not verified shot durations.

global_limits: No retention or growth outcomes were measured.
No TTS vendor/model, source-film version, music track, exact crop method or thumbnail process identified.
Contact-sheet nominal time labels may be offset within their sampling windows.
A graph preserves evidence and relationships; it does not replace unavailable media observations.
